Looking at this systematically:

**Outside view:** The series barely moves week-to-week (mean 0.58 points). Last Friday's value is the strongest predictor for most subgroups. Several subgroups show mild downward trends over the 10-week window, but the smoothed MRP model means changes are gradual. The most volatile subgroups are independents (mean abs weekly change ~2.6), males (~2.0), and age 65+ (~1.9); the most stable are Democrats (~0.3), Black voters (~0.8), and college grads (~0.9).

**Inside view:** The news cycle is consistently negative for Trump â Reuters/Ipsos at record low 32%, AP-NORC showing economic dissatisfaction, Hispanic voters souring significantly, independents favoring Democrats. This aligns with and reinforces existing downward trends, particularly for Hispanics (-44.1, declining ~2pts/week recently) and independents. However, Civiqs smoothing means the news is already partially baked in. I expect slight continued decline in trend-moving subgroups, with possible mean reversion in subgroups that had large one-week swings (age 35-49 dropped 3.8 to -40.0; race_other swung between -40.7 and -44.7).

**Pre-mortem:** The most likely failure mode is overestimating movement â the MRP smoothing dampens news-driven shifts, so even a bad news week may only move things 0.5-1 point. I've kept most forecasts within ~0.5 of last week's value, with wider SDs on volatile subgroups to account for their swinginess.

**Calibration:** SDs are set proportional to each subgroup's historical mean absolute weekly change, providing appropriate uncertainty bands.
